section: Constitutional evolution - Regulating Act 1773 to the Government of India Act 1935 (act-by-act provisions)
subsections: Government of India Act 1935 - federation, provincial autonomy, central dyarchy, Federal Court, borrowed features
Act → designation created or renamed (GG of Bengal, GG of India, Viceroy, Secretary of State)

accepted.s:
The Government of India Act, 1935 comprised:
1. 321 sections
2. 14 parts
3. 10 schedules
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Government of India Act, 1935 contained 321 sections, 14 parts and 10 schedules.
accepted.tq: Use the numerical cluster to verify all three statements together.
accepted.sec: Government of India Act 1935 - federation, provincial autonomy, central dyarchy, Federal Court, borrowed features  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to the proposed All India Federation under the Government of India Act, 1935, consider the following statements:
1. It was intended to comprise British Indian provinces and princely states.
2. Accession of princely states to the federation was compulsory.
3. The federation did not come into existence because no princely state joined it.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The federation was designed for provinces and princely states, but accession of the states was optional. Since no princely state joined, the federation never came into operation.
accepted.tq: Test the constitutional design separately from its actual implementation.
accepted.sec: Government of India Act 1935 - federation, provincial autonomy, central dyarchy, Federal Court, borrowed features  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the Government of India Act, 1935, the residuary powers were vested in the:
accepted.x: Although legislative subjects were divided into Federal, Provincial and Concurrent Lists, residuary powers were placed with the Governor-General.
accepted.tq: Ask who held the exceptional power outside the three legislative lists.
accepted.sec: Government of India Act 1935 - federation, provincial autonomy, central dyarchy, Federal Court, borrowed features  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the provincial autonomy introduced by the Government of India Act, 1935?
o: Provincial legislatures were made subordinate to the Federal Court.
All provincial subjects were reserved exclusively for the Governors.
Provinces were administered by ministers responsible to their legislatures.
Dyarchy was introduced in the provinces under the control of the Governor-General.
accepted.x: Provincial autonomy replaced provincial dyarchy with governments headed by ministers responsible to the provincial legislatures.
accepted.tq: Identify the authority to which the executive became responsible.
accepted.sec: Government of India Act 1935 - federation, provincial autonomy, central dyarchy, Federal Court, borrowed features  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The provincial autonomy provisions of the Government of India Act, 1935 came into operation in:
accepted.x: The provincial governments under the autonomy scheme took office from April 1937.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the year of enactment from the year of actual operation.
accepted.sec: Government of India Act 1935 - federation, provincial autonomy, central dyarchy, Federal Court, borrowed features  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following subjects were reserved under the proposed central dyarchy of the Government of India Act, 1935?
1. Defence
2. Foreign affairs
3. Local self-government
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Defence and foreign affairs were reserved subjects under the Governor-General. Local self-government was made a provincial subject.
accepted.tq: Separate reserved central subjects from a provincial subject.
accepted.sec: Government of India Act 1935 - federation, provincial autonomy, central dyarchy, Federal Court, borrowed features  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The central legislature proposed under the Government of India Act, 1935 was to consist of the:
o: Federal Assembly and Council of States
Legislative Assembly and Council of India
accepted.x: The bicameral central legislature was to comprise the Federal Assembly and the Council of States.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the names of the central legislative chambers.
accepted.sec: Government of India Act 1935 - federation, provincial autonomy, central dyarchy, Federal Court, borrowed features  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following sets consists entirely of provinces that had bicameral legislatures under the Government of India Act, 1935?
o: Assam, United Provinces, Central Provinces, Sindh
accepted.x: The six provinces with bicameral legislatures were Bengal, Bombay, Madras, Bihar, Assam and the United Provinces. The first option contains only members of this group.
accepted.tq: Find the option whose every member belongs to the specified six-province group.
accepted.sec: Government of India Act 1935 - federation, provincial autonomy, central dyarchy, Federal Court, borrowed features  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following provinces was NOT among the six provinces provided with bicameral legislatures under the Government of India Act, 1935?
accepted.x: Bengal, Bombay, Madras, Bihar, Assam and the United Provinces had bicameral legislatures. Punjab was not included in this group.
accepted.tq: Test the exception within a compact memorisation list.
accepted.sec: Government of India Act 1935 - federation, provincial autonomy, central dyarchy, Federal Court, borrowed features  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
The Government of India Act, 1935 extended communal representation to include which of the following groups?
1. Depressed classes
2. Women
3. Labour
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Act extended communal representation to depressed classes, women and labour in addition to existing categories.
accepted.tq: Check whether the listed social categories are all covered by the provision.
accepted.sec: Government of India Act 1935 - federation, provincial autonomy, central dyarchy, Federal Court, borrowed features  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following institutions were provided for or established under the Government of India Act, 1935?
1. Federal Court at Delhi
2. Federal, Provincial and Joint Public Service Commissions
3. Reserve Bank of India
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Act provided for the Federal Court at Delhi, Federal/Provincial/Joint Public Service Commissions and the Reserve Bank of India.
accepted.tq: Group the institutional innovations associated with one enactment.
accepted.sec: Government of India Act 1935 - federation, provincial autonomy, central dyarchy, Federal Court, borrowed features  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Joint Public Service Commission — established under the Charter Act, 1833
RBI — established under the Government of India Act, 1935
Federal Court — established at Bombay under the Government of India Act, 1919
Bicameral provincial legislatures — introduced under the Government of India Act, 1919
accepted.x: The Government of India Act, 1935 provided for the Reserve Bank of India. The other institutions or provisions are associated with different Acts or locations.
accepted.tq: Reject options by checking both the institution and the correct enactment.
accepted.sec: Government of India Act 1935 - federation, provincial autonomy, central dyarchy, Federal Court, borrowed features  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The franchise under the Government of India Act, 1935 increased from approximately 3 per cent to about:
accepted.x: The Act substantially expanded the franchise, raising it from about 3 per cent to approximately 14 per cent of the population.
accepted.tq: Compare the initial and final values rather than recalling an isolated figure.
accepted.sec: Government of India Act 1935 - federation, provincial autonomy, central dyarchy, Federal Court, borrowed features  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following territorial changes were associated with the Government of India Act, 1935?
1. Separation of Burma from India
2. Separation of Sindh from Bombay
3. Separation of Orissa from Bihar
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Act provided for Burma's separation from India, Sindh's separation from Bombay and Orissa's separation from Bihar.
accepted.tq: Combine geographically distinct territorial changes into one verification set.
accepted.sec: Government of India Act 1935 - federation, provincial autonomy, central dyarchy, Federal Court, borrowed features  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following provisions of the Government of India Act, 1935 was made a provincial subject?
accepted.x: Local self-government was made a provincial subject, whereas defence and foreign affairs were reserved under the Governor-General.
accepted.tq: Separate the provincial subject from the reserved central subjects.
accepted.sec: Government of India Act 1935 - federation, provincial autonomy, central dyarchy, Federal Court, borrowed features  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following provisions of the Government of India Act, 1935 was borrowed into the Constitution of India in substantially corresponding form?
o: The separate colonial status of Burma
The compulsory accession of princely states
accepted.x: The federal scheme, office of Governor, judiciary, Public Service Commissions, emergency provisions and administrative details were among the features carried into the Constitution. Compulsory accession and non-operational dyarchy were not borrowed as constitutional arrangements.
accepted.tq: Identify a continuing constitutional feature rather than a colonial arrangement that failed or ended.
accepted.sec: Government of India Act 1935 - federation, provincial autonomy, central dyarchy, Federal Court, borrowed features  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Section 63 of the Government of India Act, 1935, relating to the Governor's address, corresponds broadly to which Article of the Constitution of India?
accepted.x: Section 63 concerning the Governor's address became the basis of Article 175 of the Constitution of India.
accepted.tq: Match the colonial section with its corresponding constitutional Article.
accepted.sec: Government of India Act 1935 - federation, provincial autonomy, central dyarchy, Federal Court, borrowed features  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following designations in chronological order of their creation or adoption:
A. Governor-General of Bengal
B. Governor-General of India
C. Viceroy
D. Secretary of State for India
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The designation Governor-General of Bengal was created in 1773, Governor-General of India in 1833, and Viceroy and Secretary of State for India in 1858.
accepted.tq: Arrange the designations by their parent Acts and use the first and last positions.
accepted.sec: Act → designation created or renamed (GG of Bengal, GG of India, Viceroy, Secretary of State)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who was the first holder of the office of Governor-General of Bengal created by the Regulating Act, 1773?
accepted.x: Warren Hastings was the first Governor-General of Bengal under the Regulating Act, 1773.
accepted.tq: Match the office created by an Act with its first incumbent.
accepted.sec: Act → designation created or renamed (GG of Bengal, GG of India, Viceroy, Secretary of State)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Government of India Act, 1858 — Warren Hastings as Viceroy
Charter Act, 1833 — William Bentinck as Governor-General of India
Regulating Act, 1773 — Lord Canning as Governor-General of Bengal
Government of India Act, 1858 — William Bentinck as Secretary of State for India
accepted.x: The Charter Act, 1833 designated the Governor-General of Bengal as the Governor-General of India, and William Bentinck was the first holder of that office.
accepted.tq: Use the wrong-person-with-the-office trap to verify the complete pair.
accepted.sec: Act → designation created or renamed (GG of Bengal, GG of India, Viceroy, Secretary of State)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The office of Viceroy of India was created by the Government of India Act, 1858, and its first holder was:
accepted.x: The Government of India Act, 1858 created the designation Viceroy, and Lord Canning became its first holder.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the first Viceroy from the first Secretary of State and earlier Governors-General.
accepted.sec: Act → designation created or renamed (GG of Bengal, GG of India, Viceroy, Secretary of State)  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Government of India Act, 1858:
1. It created the office of the Secretary of State for India.
2. The Secretary of State was assisted by a 15-member Council of India.
3. Lord Stanley was the first holder of the office.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Act created the Secretary of State for India, assisted by a 15-member Council of India; Lord Stanley was the first Secretary of State for India.
accepted.tq: Verify the office, its assisting body and its first holder as one administrative arrangement.
accepted.sec: Act → designation created or renamed (GG of Bengal, GG of India, Viceroy, Secretary of State)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who was the first Indian and the first elected President of the Central Legislative Assembly?
accepted.x: Vithalbhai Patel became the first Indian and the first elected President of the Central Legislative Assembly in 1925. The office was later known as the Speaker.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the first Indian office-holder from other prominent constitutional figures.
accepted.sec: Act → designation created or renamed (GG of Bengal, GG of India, Viceroy, Secretary of State)  [APPSC]
